claims.text: Adding approximately 2–5 at% Si to high-purity ZrB2 powder will enable consolidation by SPS at about 1650 °C.
The Si addition will induce transient liquid-phase sintering.
Transient liquid-phase sintering will lower the effective sintering activation energy and promote densification at lower temperature.
The added Si will form a uniformly distributed, thin Si-rich grain-boundary phase.
During high-temperature oxidizing exposure, grain-boundary Si will preferentially oxidize to form a continuous SiO2 scale.
The SiO2 scale will inhibit further oxidation of the ZrB2 body.
The Si-derived protective layer will impede corrosion or penetration by liquid plating metals.
SPS under argon at about 1650 °C, with heating rates above 100 °C/min and dwell times of 5–10 minutes, is an applicable processing window.
Fast heating and short dwell times will limit grain growth.
Si-modified ZrB2 processed under the proposed conditions will have a fine, dense microstructure.
The proposed material will be mechanically robust and stronger than the comparison materials.
The proposed material will show lower high-temperature oxidation weight gain than conventional high-temperature-sintered single-phase ZrB2 and earlier lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed material will resist liquid-metal corrosion better than conventional single-phase ZrB2 and earlier lower-temperature specimens.
The expected performance applies in high-temperature oxidizing environments and liquid plating baths.
Excessive Si segregation could produce a secondary glassy phase and adversely affect phase character or mechanical properties.
